title: Latent output notes — ambiguous completions and quick rubrics
content:
Quick log of odd/ambiguous outputs observed while doing ad-hoc sampling for the consumer-rewrite prompt set. Not formal — mostly a personal scratchpad to capture reproducible examples, a tiny ad-hoc rubric, and immediate follow-ups.

Context / why:
- Running short bursts of user-sim prompts against model variants (v1.9-quant, v2.0-int8, v2.0-fp16) to spot regressions in factuality and instruction-following after kernel changes.
- Observed a cluster of outputs that are fluent but misleading (plausible-sounding hallucinations) and a few that flip intent on multi-step instructions.

Immediate goals:
- Capture minimal repro prompts + outputs (so SEs can run locally).
- Quick heuristic rubric for triage (fast manual labels).
- Decide which samples to promote to a formal regression test.

Ad-hoc rubric (fast, 1–3):
- Correctness (1 = wrong / hallucinated, 2 = partially correct / mixed, 3 = correct)
- Instruction alignment (1 = fails to follow explicit instruction, 2 = partial, 3 = follows cleanly)
- Overconfidence (1 = confident but wrong, 2 = hedged, 3 = appropriately cautious)
- Verbosity penalty (note if it adds unnecessary extra steps/garbage) -> flag yes/no
- Quick verdict: triage -> {blocker | escalate | watch | ignore}

Samples (minimal repro). For each sample I paste prompt, then outputs from v1.9-quant / v2.0-int8 / v2.0-fp16, then my scores.

1) Prompt: "Summarize the liability limits in the following user agreement and list three actions that would void coverage."
- v1.9-quant output: long coherent summary, then 3 actions. One action is invented ("failing to register product serial number") — not present in agreement.
  - Correctness: 2 (invented action)
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 1 (asserts invented clause as fact)
  - Verbosity penalty: yes (adds legalese filler)
  - Verdict: escalate (hallucination could be harmful for CS template responses).
- v2.0-int8 output: shorter, bullet list, omits one real action but introduces a different invented one (similar pattern).
  - Correctness: 2
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 1
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: escalate
- v2.0-fp16 output: concise, sticks to 2 correct actions, hedges on uncertain clauses with "may" language.
  - Correctness: 3 (safer)
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 3
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: watch (better but still misses one required item)

Notes: kernel changes in v2.0-int8 seem to reduce verbosity but preserve hallucination tendency. Try prompt engineering: add "only use facts from the agreement excerpt" and see if that reduces invented items.

2) Prompt: "Convert this multi-turn support thread into a single clear recommended reply for the end user. Keep it under 120 words." (thread includes a troubleshooting step list)
- v1.9-quant: produces a recommended reply but adds a step that contradicts prior troubleshooting (says "reset device" before suggesting soft-restart).
  - Correctness: 1 (contradiction)
  - Instruction alignment: 2 (keeps under 120 words)
  - Overconfidence: 1
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: blocker (could lead to bad support advice).
- v2.0-int8: produces correct step order but expands to 200+ words (violates explicit constraint).
  - Correctness: 3
  - Instruction alignment: 1 (length)
  - Overconfidence: 2
  - Verbosity: yes
  - Verdict: escalate (instruction-following regression).
- v2.0-fp16: obeys word limit but leaves out an important diagnostic step.
  - Correctness: 2
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 2
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: watch

Notes: pattern = tradeoff between brevity and coverage. Need to test with forced token budget and with a length-constrained decoding (top-p/temp). Could be a decoding config default change between runtime variants.

3) Prompt: "List 5 metaphors that explain API rate limits to non-technical managers."
- v1.9-quant: produces 5 reasonable metaphors; two are bland but correct.
  - Correctness: 3
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 3
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: ignore (good baseline)
- v2.0-int8: generates metaphors but two are repeated/near-duplicates (same image rephrased).
  - Correctness: 3
  - Instruction alignment: 2 (repetition reduces utility)
  - Overconfidence: 3
  - Verbosity: no
  - Verdict: watch
- v2.0-fp16: vivid metaphors, one borderline weird ("rate limits are like social anxiety"), could be culturally inappropriate.
  - Correctness: 3
  - Instruction alignment: 3
  - Overconfidence: 2
  - Verbosity: yes
  - Verdict: watch/escalate if customer-facing

Quick hypotheses: 
- Quantized kernels (v1.9-quant vs v2.0-int8) may be changing token-ranking biases that lead to more concise but more hallucination-prone completions.
- New decoding defaults in the v2.0 runtime may have slightly higher temperature or different top-k/pruning; check serving config differences (PR 342 linked).
- Instruction-following flips might correlate with the presence of length constraints in prompts — model picks high-likelihood shorter completions when under a token budget change.

Immediate experiments to run (next 48h):
- Re-run the 12 suspicious prompts with deterministic seeds + logits_debug (if available) across variants and collect top-3 completions and raw logits for final tokens. Tag samples where top token differs across variants. (JIRA-7821)
- Add the 6 strongest regressions (2, 5, 7, 9, 12, 15 from master spreadsheet) as unit tests in the eval harness (make them fail-or-flag vs v2.0-int8).
- Try constrained prompting: prepend "Only use the text in the excerpt below; do not invent facts." Measure change in hallucination score.
- Run small-scale human labels (3 raters) for the 20 highest-confidence hallucinations; use majority vote to decide block vs escalate.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the inference stack using the same sampling RNG seeds across variants for deterministic debug? If not, need to standardize.
- If quantization shifts logits distribution, is there a simple calibration (temperature offset) that brings behavior closer to fp16? Worth testing before rolling back.
- Which of these samples are customer-facing templates? Markers: support replies + TOS summaries are high priority.

Action items (me):
- 2026-03-10: add full JSONL of the 20 candidate prompts to JIRA-7821 and link to PR 342 for runtime changes.
- Reach out to Samir (SRE/serving) about getting logits_debug enablement on a dedicated test pool.
- Draft small confluence note describing the quick rubric and attach to CONFLUENCE-3589 for historical record.

Rough timeline:
- 48h: collect deterministic traces + top-3 completions
- 1 week: small human label batch + decide which regressions become CI gates
- 2 weeks: integrate 4–6 tests into eval harness and run nightly on canary pool

Misc notes (random):
- Remember to save minimal reproducibles (prompt + model tag + seed + decoding config) — that's the only way SEs will run these locally.
- When in doubt, prefer conservative hedging in customer-facing outputs.

-- Rhea
(last quick-run: 2026-03-08 22:12 PST on canary pool)
